Subject: Audit intake — initial questions for ISO/FedRAMP path

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for agreeing to an intake call next week. To help us scope the audit window and sampling ahead of the call, can you confirm the following items by EOD Aug 14? If anything is sensitive, indicate who on your side is the best control owner and we can request a secure upload link.

1) Service boundary & deployment types: list of services/enclaves in scope (hosted API, dedicated pools, private VPC), and whether production traffic is routed through all of them.
2) Control owners for: Logging (log storage & retention), Key Management (KMS/HSM), Change Management, Vulnerability Management, and Access Reviews.
3) Typical retention windows for audit-relevant artifacts: logs, snapshots, config backups, and metrics; please flag any regions with different retention.
4) Approximate client data residency requirements (if you segregate EU/US workloads).
5) Any recent infrastructure changes (past 12 months) — major migrations, new encryption-at-rest configuration, or rollout of private deployments.
6) Preferred sampling period for logs/snapshots (30/90/180 days) and whether you can provide point-in-time snapshots for enclaves.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short priorities document that outlines what auditors commonly pull for an ISO + FedRAMP intake. If you can provide the high-level inventory and the control owner list, we’ll map the sample asks to your evidence buckets and come back with a minimal request set.

Evidence upload: we can create a secure intake link for artifacts once owners are confirmed.

Regards,

Thanks — quick clarification on the sampling window: for FedRAMP compatibility we should default to a 90-day window for logs (system, access, and admin audit trails). ISO can accept a 30-day sample in many cases, but auditors will often ask for a 90-day lookback if there are recent changes.

Practical constraints: Rohan, generating point-in-time snapshots for each enclave takes about 2–3 hours per snapshot plus some coordination with on-call. We can provide a single 90-day contiguous window for the majority of enclaves, but for historic snapshots older than 60 days we may need to export from our cold archive — that adds ~24–48 hours processing.

Action items:
- Kimberly: preparing manifest of log indices + retention policies by Aug 12 (I’ll include sample query examples and the location of stored indices).
- Rohan: confirm snapshot lead time for each enclave by EOD Aug 10.

If auditors insist on a 180-day sample, we’ll need to budget additional infra ops time — flagging now.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, Logging & Monitoring
